entries.title: USPSTF Grade B: screen all adults for unhealthy alcohol use
entries.snippet: The USPSTF recommends screening for unhealthy alcohol use in primary care settings in adults 18 years or older, including pregnant women, and providing persons engaged in risky or hazardous drinking with brief behavioral counseling interventions to reduce unhealthy alcohol use. (Grade B.)
entries.source_doc: Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions (Final Recommendation 2018)
entries.applies_when: any adult ≥18 in a primary care setting
entries.demo_relevance: All four demo patients qualify; Kowalski with documented alcohol use is a direct positive-screen candidate.

entries.title: AUDIT-C is a recommended screening instrument
entries.snippet: The USPSTF identified 1- to 3-item screening instruments that have the best accuracy for assessing unhealthy alcohol use in adults 18 years or older, including the abbreviated Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test–Consumption (AUDIT-C) and the NIAAA-recommended Single Alcohol Screening Question (SASQ).
entries.source_doc: Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions (Final Recommendation 2018)
entries.applies_when: screening any adult for unhealthy alcohol use
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski's intake should include AUDIT-C; supports MASLD vs MetALD/ALD classification.

entries.title: AUDIT-C interpretation thresholds
entries.snippet: An AUDIT-C score of ≥4 in men or ≥3 in women is considered positive for unhealthy alcohol use; higher scores correspond to greater likelihood of alcohol use disorder. (NIAAA / USPSTF supporting evidence.)
entries.source_org: National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism / USPSTF evidence base
entries.source_doc: Helping Patients Who Drink Too Much: A Clinician's Guide (NIAAA); USPSTF evidence review
entries.demo_relevance: Operationalizes screen-positive logic for the copilot's intake parsing.

entries.title: Brief behavioral counseling for screen-positive adults
entries.snippet: Brief behavioral counseling interventions reduce unhealthy alcohol use in adults 18 years or older, including pregnant women. Effective interventions vary in components, length, and number of contacts but typically include feedback, motivational interviewing, and goal-setting.
entries.source_doc: Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions (Final Recommendation 2018)
entries.applies_when: adult with positive screen for risky/hazardous drinking
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski: positive AUDIT-C → brief intervention is the recommended next step alongside hepatic workup.

entries.title: Refer suspected alcohol use disorder for definitive treatment
entries.snippet: Persons whose screening suggests alcohol use disorder (AUD) should be referred for further evaluation and definitive treatment, which may include pharmacotherapy (e.g., naltrexone, acamprosate) and/or psychosocial interventions. Brief counseling alone has limited evidence in established AUD. (Paraphrased.)
entries.source_doc: Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults (USPSTF) — Practice Considerations
entries.applies_when: screen-positive adult with features of AUD (high AUDIT-C, dependence symptoms)
entries.demo_relevance: Kowalski — if AUDIT-C is high or dependence is suspected, escalate beyond brief intervention.
